rv.q: "A Bronx Tale: The New Musical," Chazz Palminteri's semi-autobiographical theatrical coming-of-age story, has been told and retold so many times that it has the ritualized feel of a folk myth - and not in a good way.
The Broadway-ish production values didn't make up for it seeming a bit worn and unnecessary —especially since the excellent film was still available (and is to this day).
Fortunately, Nick Cordero carries the musical with aplomb.
A single performer attempting to inhabit all the roles cannot breathe the same life into the action, but the evening remains a compelling vehicle for the accomplished actor.
What might have been a gut-punch melodrama ends up a half-hearted musical bildungsroman -- one that, for all its infusions of local color -- is surprisingly antiseptic.
'A Bronx Tale' provides a fun night in the theater.

cn.t: Critics find this nostalgic musical adaptation charming but familiar, praising Nick Cordero's commanding performance as Sonny and energetic choreography while noting it breaks little new ground as old-fashioned storytelling.

vs.sum: The Walter Kerr Theatre offers excellent sightlines and sound quality, making it a great venue for intimate productions. However, the comfort level is below average due to limited legroom and seat width, though the theater's Italian Renaissance-inspired decor adds to its charm.

acc.note: No elevators. All accessible seating on Orchestra level. Infrared headsets and audio induction neck loops.
